Mike Tapp has confirmed his departure as Home Office minister for migration, expressing disappointment but reaffirming his "loyalty to Keir Starmer until the end" amidst reports of internal government friction.

The junior minister's exit follows a public disagreement with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood towards the end of Sir Keir’s initial tenure.

Mr Tapp had reportedly suggested exempting care workers from Ms Mahmood’s proposed indefinite leave to remain (ILR) reforms, sparking a dispute.

Sir Keir resisted calls from the Home Secretary to dismiss Mr Tapp at the time, with Downing Street issuing a rebuke to both ministers involved in the row.

Announcing his departure on X, in a post signed off with three Union flags, the MP for Dover and Deal stated: "I am no longer the Minister for Migration and Citizenship where I was predominantly overseeing our legal migration system."

He added: "I am disappointed to be leaving government, but I have no regrets remaining loyal to Keir Starmer until the end."

Reflecting on his tenure, Mr Tapp emphasised his guiding principles, asserting: "For me, service has always meant putting the country first, and I’m proud to have approached the role with that principle at its heart."

Mr Tapp sitting with Keir Starmer ( PA )

He continued: "Every decision I made in the Home Office began with my top priority: our national security." He also articulated his vision for the system, stating: "Our immigration system is also about people. That is why compassion must sit alongside firmness, striking the right balance to protect our country, support our economy, and uphold confidence in the system."

Among his achievements, he cited "delivering the massive Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) scheme, to visa pauses and improving the Windrush Compensation Scheme," adding that "it has been truly satisfying to play a part in strengthening our immigration system."

Despite acknowledging that "net migration is falling, there is still much more to do," Mr Tapp pledged to continue contributing to Parliament, stating: "I will always put my country first and that is why I will continue to bring my experience from my time working at the highest levels of national security to Parliament."

He concluded by expressing his belief that "This Labour Government must succeed – for the good of our country. I will be working every single day to help deliver for the British people," and extended his gratitude, saying: "Thank you to my Private Office and Home Office officials who have worked hard with me to make progress."

He also wished his successor "the very best of luck." Downing Street has yet to announce who will take over the migration portfolio.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Argentina FA president ‘has phone seized as FBI grab computers’ from officials at last second before they leave USA
Sports.content:
FOOTIE PROBE Argentina FA president ‘has phone seized as FBI grab computers’ from officials at last second before they leave USA

THE president of Argentina’s FA had his phone seized by FBI agents only moments before he was about to board a flight out of the US.

This follows explosive claims that hundreds of millions of dollars in sponsorship money were laundered through US banks.



Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia was preparing to fly to Buenos Aires with several members of the World Cup squad when he was surrounded by US law enforcement.

Tapia was taken into custody at JFK International airport in New York and told to hand over all of his electronic devices.



Sources say the authorities also seized phones and computers from other members of the Argentine delegation.

The flight – which had been scheduled to leave at 6.00am – eventually took off around 8.15am.

This had the knock-on effect of delaying the team’s arrival at Ezeiza International Airport, where thousands of fans were waiting.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has since released a statement denying the covert operation took place.



“It is categorically false,” the statement said.

“None of the described incidents occurred.”

Prosecutors are examining whether cash linked to the AFA was moved through American banks in a way that could amount to money laundering and fraud.

Investigators are now trying to establish exactly where the money went, who received it and whether any US laws were broken along the way.

According to court documents, Tapia will now appear before the Southern District Court of Florida.



He has also been asked to provide all information he possesses related to Tourprodenter, including communications with Pablo Toviggino, Diego Lucero, and Javier Faroni.

Tourprodenter – managed by Faroni – is a Florida-based company that handled payments linked to some of Argentina football’s biggest commercial deals.

All of them are under investigation as part of a case focusing on the financial structure of the AFA’s international commercial contracts.

Bank records allegedly show that millions of dollars passed through several accounts across various US financial institutions.

The statements are said to show that some of the money remained in the accounts for a few days before being transferred elsewhere.



Private flights, transportation, fuel, consulting, multimillion-dollar transfers to companies with little to no known commercial activity have also reportedly been identified.

Lionel Messi was not part of the group who travelled with Tapia.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, Messi travelled to Argentina a day later, before spending time at home with his family in Rosario.

An investigation is ongoing to determine whether any of the transactions constitute a crime under US law.

Sports.title: Mateus Fernandes scores ‘greatest goal ever seen’ in first start for Tottenham after £85m transfer
Sports.content:
MATEUS FERNANDES scored a wonder strike for Spurs on his debut as fans were left raving about “the greatest goal I’ve ever seen”.

Tottenham’s new £85million man was handed his first start for the club in their pre-season friendly against MK Dons on Wednesday evening.

Scroll down to see clip of wonder-goal



Fernandes, who has arrived from relegated West Ham, lashed in a venomous shot on the volley from outside the box.



The effort pinged into the net off the post and the Portugal star was immediately mobbed by his new team-mates.

The superb hit was enough to seal a 1-0 win over the League One outfit in the behind-closed-doors friendly at Hotspur Way.



But the low-key nature of the game couldn’t stop excited Spurs fans from hailing Fernandes and his technique.

One supporter posted a clip of the video and wrote: “Mateus Fernandes with the greatest goal I’ve ever seen.”

Another added: “Goal of the season and the season hasn’t even started yet.”

A third said: “Give West Ham another £85m for that alone.”



Other ambitious fans joked: “I’ve seen enough, we are winning the Premier League.”

Fernandes was asked about the strike by club media after the game and claimed it was the best goal he’s ever scored.

He said: “It was great, no? It was my favourite goal of my career by a mile. The second one was last season.

“I need to do this more, to shoot outside the box. I know I can do it.”

Spurs won the race to sign Fernandes after beating Manchester United to his signature.



He enjoyed a top season for the Hammers after scoring three goals and assisting four.

But he could not prevent the team’s relegation as they finished 18th, two points off Tottenham in 17th.

Sports.title: Arsenal get William Saliba injury update as star ‘makes surgery decision’ following World Cup blow
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fear William Saliba will miss MONTHS of the new season after deciding not to undergo surgery to overcome his back problem.

The defender, 25, was forced off during France’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain last week.



And there have been concerns that Saliba is in line to be crocked for the start of Arsenal’s Premier League title defence.

The former Marseille man has been weighing up how to get himself back to full fitness.



L’Equipe report Saliba has chosen not to go under the knife after holding talks with Arsenal’s medical department.

It means the centre-back is facing a lengthy period of treatment and needs to rest before being given the green light to return to training.

Saliba wants to keep tabs on the healing process and see how quickly he progresses instead of having an operation.

There have been suggestions he suffered a back fracture during Arsenal’s loss to Bournemouth in April.

But Saliba was determined to play through the pain barrier to keep his World Cup dreams alive and feature in the final weeks of the Gunners’ push for silverware.

The Emirates Stadium favourite said: “I’ve had some minor niggles for several months.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“I’ve been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League. But the coaching staff are handling it very well.

“The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you’ve got to grit your teeth.

“I’m not at 100 per cent, but there are plenty of players who aren’t at 100 per cent either. You can’t make excuses.”

Saliba’s injury has resulted in Arsenal considering a move for free agent John Stones as a short-term fix.

The six-time Premier League title winner, 32, is assessing his options after leaving Manchester City.



But Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is facing competition from Chelsea as the new season edges closer.

Sports.title: Newly single Spain hero Ferran Torres and glam singer, 29, ‘spend World Cup after party flirting and teasing’
Sports.content:
SPAIN’S World Cup hero Ferran Torres was reportedly seen flirting with singer Ana Mena while celebrating the team’s famous triumph.

The Barcelona star, 26, is on a high after netting Spain’s winner to secure a 1-0 victory over Argentina in Sunday’s final.



Torres has become a national treasure in the process and he has been lapping up the team’s celebrations in Madrid.

The winger partied with his team-mates during their open-top bus parade in the Spanish capital that ended in the Plaza de Cibeles.



Spain stars then enjoyed an after party, with Mena also securing an invite after performing on stage.

Torres is a newly-single man after rumours that he broke up with girlfriend Martina Hunter during the World Cup.



Spanish journalist Javi de Hoyos claimed the couple split just before Spain’s 2-1 win over Belgium in the quarter-finals on July 10.

And it seems Torres is moving on quickly after being spotted with Mena during the Spain team’s celebrations.

And Mena’s fellow singer Amor Romeira – who was also at the party – confirmed there was “flirting” between the pair.

She said in a response to a fan on Instagram: “There was flirting, some teasing.

Meanwhile, reporter Gerard Romero said the pair had “very good chemistry” together after speaking on Twitch stream.

He also pointed out that Mena was later seen wearing a Spain shirt with the No 7 on it that he believes belongs to Torres.

Romero said on his stream: “Last night, at the party where Ozuna was, where Myke Towers, Lola Índigo, and Ana Mena were… what jersey was Ana Mena wearing, what number was on it?”

Sports.title: Alex Scott ‘picks preferred team’ as Man Utd, Chelsea and Arsenal circle for £80m-rated Bournemouth star
Sports.content:
ALEX SCOTT reportedly wants to seal a mega-money move to Chelsea instead of Manchester United or Arsenal.

The Bournemouth midfielder, 22, put his admirers on red alert after rejecting a new contract at the Vitality Stadium.



And Chelsea tried to tempt the Cherries into selling Scott for £64million, only for the bid to be turned down.

But it appears the former Bristol City man has not given up on completing a dream switch to Stamford Bridge.



The Standard report Scott has pinpointed Chelsea as his preferred destination this summer.

His stance will come as a huge blow for Man Utd and Arsenal, who have shown interest.

The Gunners were already beaten by Chelsea to the £117m signing of Morgan Rogers earlier this week.

And Arsenal supremo Mikel Arteta will be seething if he misses out on another transfer target to Blues chief Xabi Alonso.

But Bournemouth have been desperately attempting to tie Scott down to an improved deal.

New boss Marco Rose, who is preparing for his first season in charge after succeeding Andoni Iraola, sees the talisman as a key part of his plans.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Bournemouth have attempted to price their sought-after star out of a move by rating him at £80m.

Scott played a pivotal role in the Cherries bagging European qualification for the first time in their history last season.

He made 37 Premier League appearances in the record-breaking campaign, notching three goals and an assist along the way.

That form resulted in Scott being rewarded with the chance to join England’s training camp before the World Cup.



It softened the blow after he was not included in the Three Lions’ 26-man squad for the tournament.

Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is with Manchester United Women, leading to Old Trafford chiefs hoping she could convince him to head north.

Sports.title: Inter Miami announce signing of former Man Utd star Casemiro but transfer is immediately investigated by MLS
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO has completed a move to Inter Miami – but the switch has landed the MLS side in hot water.

The midfielder, 34, was a free agent after walking away from Manchester United at the end of last season.



And Casemiro, who broke down in tears as he made an emotional farewell speech to Red Devils fans, has penned a one-year deal which has the option of being extended until 2029.

But MLS chiefs have confirmed the transfer is being investigated due to concerns of potentially violating tampering rules.



LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights, which led to Inter Miami facing the threat of having to shell out £750,000.

A probe has now been launched to decide whether the Brazilian’s new employers violated regulations to get the deal over the line.



An MLS statement read: “Major League Soccer is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami CF.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete.

“While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.”

The size of the fee Inter Miami will pay LA Galaxy for Casemiro’s discovery rights is set to be decided after the investigation.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The reigning MLS Cup champions were fined more than $2million after being found guilty of ignoring salary cap rules in 2021.

It led to co-owner Jorge Mas being forced to pay $250,000 out of his own pocket and sporting director Paul McDonough was suspended for a year.

But Casemiro, who missed out on World Cup glory after Brazil were knocked out by Norway in the last-16, has not joined Inter Miami as a designated player.

Mas said: “Casemiro’s arrival reflects the vision and ambition that define Inter Miami.



“We never settle. We’re always looking to grow, improve and raise our standards every season.

“We’ve built a global club with the vision of becoming not only the best club in the United States, but also a benchmark globally.”

Casemiro, who made 34 Premier League appearances for United last season, will now have Lionel Messi among his team-mates.

The Real Madrid legend won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup during his time at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho becomes third Man Utd flop to join Aston Villa in three years and completes medical for Chelsea loan
Sports.content:
ALEJANDRO GARNACHO is closing in on a loan move to Aston Villa after completing a medical.

The winger is set to become the third Red Devils flop to join the club in three years after falling out of favour at Chelsea.



He only signed for the Blues last summer after falling out with old boss Ruben Amorim at Old Trafford.

Garnacho follows Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford in trying his luck at Villa Park after a lack of game time.



Rashford had relative success at Villa during his loan spell in 2024-25 as he scored twice and assisted four in the second half of the campaign.

Sancho effectively replaced Rashford the following season after he flopped on loan at Chelsea the previous year.



But the move didn’t go as well for the ex-Borussia Dortmund star as he managed just one goal and three assists across the whole season.

Garnacho will hope to fare better under Unai Emery, who has reportedly been chasing the player since before he joined Chelsea, according to the Athletic.

Villa have agreed a loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy as they look to replace Morgan Rogers – who has headed the other way in a £117m British record deal.

And a four-year contract is in place should the buy option be executed next summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He will become the fourth player to arrive at Villa Park this summer after Johan Manzambi, Joao Gomes and Modou Keba Cisse.

The transaction is a tricky one for Villa after selling Rogers to Chelsea for a record price.

UEFA’s rules mean that any permanent signing from Chelsea would count as a “player exchange transaction”.

That means the profit from the Rogers deal would be reduced based on the difference in fees between him and Garnacho.



UEFA’s period for players exchanges covers a 45-day period and there are only 41 days left in the transfer window.

So Villa’s workaround is to agree a conditional loan move that be made permanent next summer.

That also works for Chelsea, who will be able to retain more profit on the Garnacho deal.

Villa are looking to avoid more trouble with Uefa after being fined £19.4million for a “significant breach” of its squad cost rules.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s pre-season plans revealed with 14 players on post-World Cup holidays, Marbella camp and old-school friendlies
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have officially started pre-season this week as they get ready to defend their Premier League crown.

The Gunners lifted the title for the first time in 22 years last season and are determined to retain it.

Mikel Arteta has worked with staff to put together a plan that will get his players up to speed for the new campaign.



Arsenal begin their defence of the Prem on August 21, when they host Coventry City, and want to hit the ground running.



Who is already in training?

Arsenal had 15 players at the World Cup this summer, which means not many of last season’s squad are training right now.

Ben White, who injured his knee in May, is one of them and he is back in full training.

Jurrien Timber is stepping up his rehab after a minor operation last month and hopes to play some part in pre-season.

Those not at the World Cup and now in training include the likes of Christian Norgaard, Cristhian Mosquera, Gabriel Jesus, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Riccardo Calafiori.

Ethan Nwaneri, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson have also reported for duty after being on loan last season.

New signing Illan Meslier has also got to work and is training alongside fellow goalkeepers Kepa Arrizabalaga and Tommy Setford.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Teenage stars Marli Salmon and Max Dowman are with the first team, too, and could get plenty of minutes in pre-season.



When are the World Cup stars back?

Fifa rules state that players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off during the summer break.

Arsenal had 15 players over in North America this summer and they will return at different times, depending on when they exited the World Cup.

One of those – Leandro Trossard – has already left after joining Besiktas for around £17million earlier this month.

Eight of Arsenal’s squad made it to the final weekend of the World Cup and therefore will not be due back to training until August 10 at the earliest.

That group includes England quartet Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.



Spain trio David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino are also part of it, as is France’s William Saliba.

There is a chance they are given more than three weeks off, with Arsenal’s first Prem game not until August 21, and players’ return dates will be decided on a case-by-case basis.

Arsenal’s six other players at the World Cup this summer were Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Piero Hincapie and Viktor Gyokeres.

The two Gabriels, Havertz, Hincapie and Gyokeres all went out before the quarter-finals of the World Cup – and so should return to training next week.

Odegaard and Norway made it to the last 8 and so a three-week break for him would see the Gunners skipper back in early August.



What do Arsenal have planned?

Arsenal officially started pre-season on Monday, although they held a mini training camp in Marbella last week.

Arteta has organised a similar event in the past and did so again this year, inviting players to bring their families along, too.

Arsenal have kept their pre-season plans low key this summer after a gruelling season that was 63 games long.

They have also started later than other sides due to having 15 players at the World Cup and last season not finishing until May 30.

They are not going on a farflung tour across the globe and instead will head to Spain later this month for a proper training camp.



That will coincide with the Gunners having their first friendly of the summer at Girona on August 1.

Four days later, they will take on Real Betis in Dublin before flying back to London for two friendlies at the Emirates.

They are taking on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on August 9 and then host Como three days later.

All of that is designed to get Arsenal ready and firing for the Community Shield with Manchester City in Cardiff on August 16.

What new faces are there and will more be coming?

Arsenal have made Hincapie’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent for £34.5million and signed Meslier on a free transfer after his contract with Leeds expired.



Christos Tzolis is undergoing a medical this week and will join from Club Brugge for a fee of £34m.

The winger has already played friendlies for Brugge this summer and so is ready to get work with Arsenal.

The club are working on more signings and still want to add a defender, midfielder and forward.

There have been changes to the medical department over the summer and the new staff are running sessions this week.

The new hires include Arnaldo Abrantes joining from Aston Villa as club doctor.



Eneko Angulo arrives from Real Betis as a rehabilitation specialist and Bayer Leverkusen fitness coach Jose Jimenez has been added to the ranks as well.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They have come in after club doctor Zafar Iqbal and head of sports science and performance Tom Allen both left.

Sam Wilson, lead physical performance coach, has also departed after being poached by Italian side Parma.

Inter Miami have secured the signing of Casemiro but the MLS are reviewing the move following allegations from LA Galaxy, who had the rights to negotiate with the player

The MLS has announced they are reviewing Casemiro's move to Inter Miami following allegations of tampering.

The Brazilian was allowed to leave Manchester United following the expiration of his contract at the end of last season and had a number of offers, but has chosen to move across the Atlantic and join the franchise co-owned by David Beckham.

ESPN reports that the allegation has come from LA Galaxy, ironically the club Beckham played for, who have expressed issue with the contact Inter Miami had with Casemiro before acquiring the player's Discovery Priority.

Sports.title: Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'

Jo Wilson endured the traumatic experience of being told her cancer had returned this year, despite the Sky Sports News presenter having been given the all clear years earlier

View Image Jo Wilson is aiming to raise awareness after receiving an incorrect cancer diagnosis

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has opened up about the emotional impact it has had on her upon receiving a second, incorrect cancer diagnosis, just three years after being declared all clear following her year‑long battle with stage three cervical cancer. The 41-year-old has documented her journey with the disease.

‌



She was first diagnosed in June 2022 after a routine smear test, which led to her undergoing life‑saving radiotherapy and chemotherapy treatment. Wilson produced a documentary highlighting football figures who had also faced cancer battles titled 'Football, Cancer and Me,' which was released in November 2025.

‌



On Tuesday, Wilson took to Instagram to raise awareness after being told this year that her cancer had returned. In a touching post where she shared several photos from the hospital, she wrote: "A little life update, please read until the end (red heart emoji).

‌



Man Utd and Arsenal locked in £40million transfer battle as duo hold talks over deal READ MORE :

5 attackers Arsenal could still sign after Morgan Rogers transfer setback READ MORE :

"In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn't believe it - it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again. But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct.

"What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all. The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma - a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan. The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing - then not knowing if my cancer had returned.

"Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard. On the outside, life carried on - I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos. But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.

‌



"So why am I sharing this? Firstly, because we often talk about being 'cancer free', but I'm not sure any of us ever truly feel free of it. The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality. If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The presenter continued: "Secondly, because social media is never the full picture. The last few months on here have probably looked like lots of happy moments, lovely places and time with people I love - and those moments were all real. But they existed alongside this. Instagram is a highlight reel, not the whole story.

‌



"And finally, because we never really know what someone else is carrying. A friend, a colleague, the person serving you coffee or standing next to you in the supermarket - they could be fighting a battle you know nothing about. So this is simply a reminder to be kind. Always (red heart emoji). Thank you to my incredible support network, you know who you are."

In her documentary, Wilson revealed that the diagnosis had changed her life 'in an instant', coming just shortly after the birth of her daughter Mabel.

"It hit me like a truck," she said. "I did wonder if I'm going to die. I'd prepared myself for the worst, I think you have to.

‌



"I actually didn't tell anyone. I didn't want to put it on anyone. If one person can see this and make a phone call to the doctor because something doesn't feel right, then it's worth talking about."

She underwent daily radiotherapy, weekly chemotherapy and three days of invasive internal brachytherapy across a five‑week period. It meant being separated from her daughter, a period she described as the 'darkest' phase of her illness.

‌



The broadcaster, who joined Sky Sports in 2011, has urged women to book their cervical smear test in light of her own cancer diagnosis. Around one in 130 women in the UK will be diagnosed with cervical cancer in their lifetime, yet one in three do not attend their smear test.

"I must raise awareness," she previously said. "I want people to talk about what’s stopping them from going to their tests.

"Is it finding time? Is it embarrassment? Whatever support you need, or why you ever haven’t gone for a smear - go and be tested. I promise you, it’s far better than going through cancer."

Sports.title: 5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain
Sports.content:
It is easy to think that the World Cup kicks into life and transfers just fade into the background - but that's far from being the case.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was happy for players to conduct their transfer dealings provided it didn't interfere with the team's plans, which is exactly what Elliot Anderson did as he secured a club-record move to Manchester City.

But what about the moves that didn't involve nine-figure sums changing hands? Don't think for a second that clubs sat waiting for the World Cup's hidden gems to reveal themselves, oh no, they've been working away and getting deals done.

Xabi Alonso has made his first Chelsea signing and amid all the noise about their best players leaving Newcastle have actually spent more than £40million on new talent.

‌



Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Liverpool confident of beating Arsenal to £100m star as they move on second winger READ MORE :

Now that the tournament in North America is over and players have shown what they can do on the biggest stage deals are expected to ramp up. Morgan Rogers' British-record move to Chelsea an example. Bradley Barcola, Yan Diomande, Ferran Torres and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all end up being the subjects of some mega money moves.

But here's a number of deals you may well have missed whilst watching the World Cup as clubs up and down the Premier League look to bolster their ranks.

Illan Meslier - Leeds to Arsenal, free

Arsenal have been in the market for a new back-up goalkeeper and have landed Illan Meslier, who was available on a free after his contract at Leeds expired. He was once highly-rated when he first became a fixture in the Whites starting XI, but his error count continued to increase and he was dropped at Elland Road. He was unable to force his way back in, but at 26 still has time to forge a career somewhere, even if he is due to play understudy to David Raya at the Emirates.

View 3 Images Illan Meslier was dropped after costing Leeds in the past (Image: Richard Lee/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



Marco Palestra - Atalanta to Chelsea, £47m

Alonso is the new man in charge at Chelsea and the Blues are no strangers to the transfer market. They landed Atalanta full-back Marco Palestra, who was set to move to Inter Milan before the Premier League side showcased their financial power by securing his services.

He was previously named the Serie A Defender of the Year off the back of an impressive season on loan at Cagliari and the 21-year-old was signed at the request of Alonso with Palestra capable of playing in a back four and a back three.

Bazoumana Toure - Hoffenheim to Newcastle, £43m

Newcastle's transfer window has been a disaster - selling Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali whilst they also missed out on Victor Munoz, who opted for Liverpool instead. But they did manage to secure a deal for Hoffenheim's Ivorian winger Bazoumana Toure.

They paid good money to land the 20-year-old, who came up 12 assists in Germany last season, and they will hope to see him blossom over the coming years.

‌



View 3 Images Bazoumana Toure has made a move to Newcastle

Harry Wilson - Fulham to Leeds, free

The Welshman continued to make headlines last term as he came up with big goal after big goal, several of them showcasing real quality - and every time he or his then manager were asked if and when he would sign a new deal at Fulham.

Wilson ultimately decided against and sought a new challenge with Leeds, who consolidated themselves in the top flight last term, winning the race for a player who landed 11 goals and a further eight assists in all competitions last season.

Alvaro Rodriguez - Elche to Bournemouth, £26m

The Cherries, now in Europe for the first time, are becoming one of the best in the business when it comes to signing unknown talents who go on to be successes. They've now landed Elche striker Alvaro Rodriguez, a Uruguayan who came through Real Madrid's academy.

‌



He still caught the eye despite playing for a team battling relegation, coming up with 12 goal contributions. Bournemouth maintain their top players are going nowhere, so he will compliment their leading lights.

Sports.title: Clarke Carlisle in emotional mental health plea to football fans after battling demons
Sports.content:
Clarke Carlisle in emotional mental health plea to football fans after battling demons

Fans across the UK have been urged to support one another in the new season by former QPR, Leeds United, Watford and Burnley defender Clarke Carlisle, who previously attempted to take his own life

View 3 Images Kevin Miles, Chair of Blyth Spartans, and Clarke Carlisle, Chair of Mind

Ex-Premier League ace Clarke Carlisle has urged fans to look out for each other as the new season approaches. The 46-year-old racked up over 400 professional appearances and earned three caps for the England under-21 national team.

‌



But during his playing career, and after he hung up his boots, the former defender suffered serious mental health challenges. Carlisle admitted he attempted to take his own life when he was hit by a lorry in December 2014.

‌



Carlisle is now Chair of Mind - the UK’s leading mental health charity - and is looking to challenge stigma and drive change across sport and society.

‌



Last weekend, Mind and five non-league clubs came together for a charity tournament in Northumberland - 'The Better Together Cup'.

The two-day event was organised by QTS Data Centers and Blyth Spartans in the name of celebrating grassroots football and promoting mental health.

Inside mental health campaign changing lives for footballers with autism and disabilities READ MORE :

QTS, who are building one of Europe's largest data centres in nearby Cambois, made a £20,000 donation to support the charity's work expanding mental health services across the region.

‌



Carlisle insists it's crucial to keep the mental health conversation going - and the football community can play an important role in making that happen.

"Each generation has their own new and unique challenges," he said. "But football clubs offer such a perfect environment to bring people and communities together. Without doubt, unequivocally, we are better together.

"Supporters come and watch football for their release. Any challenge or difficulty, this is an opportunity for people to get away from that and lose themselves, for 90 minutes at least.

‌



View 3 Images Clarke Carlisle named his toughest opponent in the Premier League (Image: Sam Bagnall - AMA/Getty Images)

"And because of that, football clubs also offer a fertile stomping ground to engage with fans on a meaningful one-to-one level about their mental health.

"There are still so many misconceptions. Just like our physical health, no one is immune from averse mental health.

‌



"These are issues that affect the brain and the body, the emotional and the psychological - everybody is susceptible. Although just because we are susceptible doesn't mean that it's inevitable.

"We have to keep changing the narrative - especially the classic one around male identity - that you don't show signs of weakness."

Before the World Cup, Newcastle and England star Dan Burn spoke openly about his own struggles with depression and anxiety. The 34-year-old sought out therapy during his early career and credits it with saving him from a "downward spiral".

‌



Burn, who played youth football at Blyth Spartans, continues to raise awareness in the North East. Carlisle has hailed the Three Lions ace for speaking out.

View 3 Images Dan Burn spoke out during the World Cup (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"It's really positive to see people who are in the public eye, with a public profile, discussing openly their mental health issues because it does normalise that conversation," added Carlisle, who had stints at Queens Park Rangers, Leeds, Watford, and Burnley.

‌



"Having shared my experience, people have said to me: 'I've watched you play in the Premier League. I didn't think it could've been an issue for you.'

"If you are experiencing something, you don't have to be like me or Dan Burn. You don't have to tell everybody - but it's imperative that you do tell somebody at the right time.

"So, if you want it to be your business, excellent. But make it your business with the right support. Let's put all the dots on the page so any individual can control their own picture or solution."

‌



The Better Together Cup forms part of QTS's Better Together campaign, launched in 2025 to serve the communities around its Cambois data centre campus and Northumberland.

Rita Patel Miller, Social Strategy Director at QTS, said: “Seeing clubs, fans and families fill Croft Park around such an important cause was heartwarming. We are proud to be a small part of this community.”

Kevin Miles and his family moved to Blyth in 1967, so close to Croft Park that “you could see the turnstiles from our front gate”.

Article continues below

Now the Chair of Blyth Spartans, Miles said: "The atmosphere across the weekend was electric, and the whole club felt it. To see Croft Park packed for a cause that matters so much to people here made everyone incredibly proud."

Sports.title: Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star
Sports.content:
Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star

Manchester United have made moves as they look to sign Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni even if reports claim the midfielder has signed a new deal with Los Blancos

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni has been linked with a move to Manchester (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United have enquired about Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni despite reports that the Frenchman has signed a new deal in Spain.

‌



The Red Devils remain in the market for midfield additions despite already bringing in Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively. Tchouameni would be their most blockbuster signing if they could get a deal of the line.

‌



The 26-year-old will have some down time after the World Cup before reporting for pre-season, but new Real boss Jose Mourinho has no interest in selling.

‌



Tchouameni is under contract at the Bernabeu until 2028, but there is speculation suggesting he's agreed a new contract to 2031, although nothing has been announced. Nevertheless The Sun claims those on the red side of Manchester have made moves as they bid to sign the ex-Monaco man.

Liverpool confident of beating Arsenal to £100m star as they move on second winger READ MORE :

Tchouameni is a specialist defensive midfielder and United are in the market for a player of that ilk to replace Casemiro, who was allowed to leave following the expiry of his contract.

United's midfield has been their priority this summer with Kobbie Mainoo among the only names who was present last year guaranteed to be part of Michael Carrick's plans. Manuel Ugarte's future is unclear but his injury could make him difficult to sell.

‌



The club enjoyed huge success with their recruitment 12 months ago, when attack was their priority. They went after proven Premier League quality in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, who both proved to be hits. Tielemans and Santos also know the league - with Tchouameni a potential overseas buy.

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans joined Man Utd earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

United were offered the chance to sign Tchouameni back in 2021 when he was still on Monaco's books, but did not have the budget for a midfielder. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge at Old Trafford at the time, was keen on recruiting a young midfielder and had Declan Rice as his favoured target.

Article continues below

Talk of Real cashing in on Tchouameni has ramped up since the World Cup, where Rodri was named the tournament's best player after Spain claimed glory. The Manchester City midfielder was the Ballon d'Or winner only two years ago and he's been heavily linked with a move to the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers announcement shows Chelsea have already changed under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers announcement shows Chelsea have already changed under Xabi Alonso

The £117million acquisition of the England midfielder shows a shift in Chelsea's transfer policy that bodes well for the prospect of a realistic title challenge next season

View 3 Images Xabi Alonso was hugely influential in Morgan Rogers' decision to join Chelsea (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

It is a simple photograph but one that should fire up optimism in every Chelsea fan out there, with Xabi Alonso and Morgan Rogers lighting up the room with their smiles. Alonso and Rogers - not a sporting director in sight.

‌



So many of the myriad signings made during this ownership’s tenure have seemed like business enterprises rather than footballing enterprises. So many have seemed like projects dreamt up by the moneymen and agents, having nothing to do with the man who needs to put a decent team out on the pitch.

‌



But the £117million acquisition of Rogers seems like a pure footballing move, driven by Alonso, who is the manager AND the coach. If they tempt John Stones to Stamford Bridge, it will be a pure footballing move, just as it will be if they buy Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

‌



This is Alonso making his mark. The only thing you can see Rogers doing under the guidance of Alonso - one of the most accomplished midfielders the Premier League has seen - is flourishing.

Can Argentina Premier League players have visas revoked after World Cup uproar? READ MORE :

It might well have been a fairly crude psychological ploy to provoke a reaction from the Real Madrid man but there was a time when Thomas Tuchel preferred Rogers to Jude Bellingham. And Rogers never let Tuchel down. Rogers never let England down.

Rogers turns 24 on Sunday and has plenty of developing to do, especially now he will be in harness with great friend, Cole Palmer. Rogers’ words on Palmer were more reasons for supporter optimism.

‌



“He is non-stop ringing my phone, texting me, and I can’t wait. I think that’s probably the most special thing, playing with one of your best friends and being around him every day. It’s something I’m really excited about.”

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers shares a goal celebration with his great friend Cole Palmer (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

And something Chelsea fans should be very excited about, not least for the fact that it underlines Palmer’s commitment to the club, which was not always taken for granted by sections of the fanbase.

‌



Chelsea are also one of the clubs bidding for the services of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who would be a hugely dependable replacement for Enzo Fernandez if they can get a nine-figure fee for the Argentinian.

Rogers, possibly Stones, possibly Scott - these are established Premier League performers. Obviously, the fee for Rogers is on the big side, to say the least. But Rogers brings a versatility that Alonso will love.

If Alonso uses the back-three system that served him so well at Bayer Leverkusen, there could be the mouthwatering prospect of Palmer and Rogers lining up as dual number 10s. In 55 appearances for Aston Villa last season, Rogers contributed 14 goals and 12 assists.

‌



View 3 Images Chelsea are interested in signing free agent John Stones (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Across his last two seasons, Rogers has 18 Premier League goals and 16 Premier League assists. Those are very good numbers.

A lucrative seven-year deal obviously had a lot to do with Rogers’ choice of club but it is also clear that working with the manager had something to do with it. There can be no doubt Alonso is a draw-card for potential signings and knowing Chelsea, there will be more of those this summer.

Article continues below

There will also be plenty of outgoings, all of whom will be shipped out with Alonso’s blessing. In other words, it will be good, conventional transfer market business for a good, conventional manager.

He has not managed a game yet but the immediate impact of Alonso’s arrival has been to make a dysfunctional club look like a functional challenger once again. How Alonso and Chelsea actually perform in terms of performance and results remains to be seen but it will be one of the Premier League’s more compelling narratives, that is for sure.

Sports.title: Aston Villa agree deal to sign Garnacho
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

The arrangement is for a loan with a conditional obligation to buy, which is easily achievable.

The total package, including the loan fee, is understood to meet Chelsea's valuation.

Sky Sports News has been reporting Chelsea wanted £42.6m for the winger.

Garnacho joined Chelsea last summer from Manchester United for £40m.

The Argentina international winger had not reported for pre-season training at Chelsea in order to allow him to pursue a move away.

The deal comes after the two clubs negotiated a British-record transfer fee of £117m for Morgan Rogers to go in the other direction.

Why UEFA rules make Garnacho move complicated

The deal for Garnacho to move from Chelsea to Aston Villa is not a straightforward one.

Both clubs were recently fined by UEFA for breaching financial sustainability regulations. They are walking a fine tightrope to avoid further heavier sanctions. Last year, Chelsea entered a four-year settlement agreement with UEFA and therefore remain subject to UEFA's stricter financial guidelines - despite not being in European competition this season.

Villa were able to bank an enormous profit from the sale of Morgan Rogers to Chelsea. A profit which will go a long way to ensuring they are compliant with both UEFA and the Premier League's differing financial constraints this season. But the club also need to rebuild their squad following multiple departures to ensure they are ready to compete on all fronts this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Transfer Talk Podcast, Henry Winter discusses why Aston Villa should be wary of signing Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea

Garnacho was made available for transfer by Chelsea this summer. Villa were looking for a winger. Unai Emery admired the Argentinian. A permanent deal would seem straightforward.

However, that would compromise Villa when it comes to booking that huge British transfer record fee from Chelsea. That's because of UEFA guidelines which - to simplify slightly - deem that two players being transferred in opposite directions counts as a 'player exchange transaction' if a) they are concluded in 45 days of each other and b) have the same or similar payment obligations, deadlines or dates.

If the Garnacho and Rogers deals were deemed as a single player exchange transaction, then Villa's profit would be reduced in UEFA calculations to the net difference in fees. Chelsea were seeking £42.6m for Garnacho this summer. Easy to see how much of a chunk that would take out of the Rogers profit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Ron Walker explains how Chelsea can afford to pay £117m for Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers

So how about a loan with an obligation to buy? A mechanism that allows Chelsea to guarantee they achieve a permanent sale but circumvents the player exchange transaction rules. Sadly, that wouldn't work either. UEFA are clamping down on the multitude of loopholes that previously existed. They deem that if a 'condition is considered to be virtually certain, then the player's registration must be recognised by both clubs as a permanent transfer from the inception of the loan agreement'. Therefore, we'd still have a player exchange transaction.

So, the deal struck for Garnacho to join Villa appears to work for all parties - sort of. Chelsea believe the conditions to make Garnacho's move to Villa permanent are 'easily achievable'.

However, there still remains a small risk for the Blues. There has to be enough jeopardy in the deal to ensure UEFA are satisfied that a permanent move is not a foregone conclusion from the outset. The Blues will hope there's no repeat of what happened to Harvey Elliott at Villa Park last season. A talented player left warming the bench as his main employers watch his future selling price plummet.

Therefore, seeing a resurgent Alejandro Garnacho flying down the left wing in claret and blue will be a good sight for both Villa and Chelsea.

Is Garnacho the right fit on the left for Aston Villa?

Image: Garnacho celebrates scoring for Chelsea against Wrexham

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

In a tough first season for Chelsea, Garnacho struggled to make much of an impact in an already overcrowded left-hand side. The Argentine managed just 1,217 Premier League minutes across his 25 appearances last term, an average of less than 49 minutes per game.

That is less than both Rogers (1,528) and Emiliano Buendia (1,527} managed in the same position while sharing the workload off the left flank for Villa last season.

Their average returns were far more superior too. Garnacho's five goal involvements saw him average one every 243 minutes compared to Rogers' record of a goal involvement every 90 minutes, and Buendia's of every 190.

Should Villa bring in Garnacho, it would surely mean a tweak in Unai Emery's system when the Argentine is on the pitch.

With Buendia and Rogers, there is a versatility that not only sees them able to play on either flank, but also show a tendency to move inside.

Garnacho has operated on the right-hand side previously. He scored a goal in the FA Cup final win for Manchester United over local rivals City while operating from that flank. Cut inside though? That is something you see far less from the winger.

His tendency is to hug the touchline and stay wide. In doing so, it would mean that Emery would need to be flexible with his attacking patterns, or Garnacho would have to show adaptability. Which is more likely?

Sports.title: Casemiro joins Inter Miami on free transfer
Sports.content:
Casemiro has joined Inter Miami on a free transfer after leaving Manchester United.

The Brazil international has signed a deal that will see him through to the end of the 2027 MLS season and also includes an option to extend the contract until 2029.

Casemiro spent four years at Old Trafford, scoring in the League Cup final victory in 2023 and reaching two FA Cup finals, winning the competition in 2024. He was also part of the United side that reached the Europa League final in May 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Casemiro and Michael Carrick addressed the home crowd at Manchester's United final home game of last season as many players bade farewell

"What motivates me the most, and I think this is true for every player, is winning and continuing to grow. The project the club presented to me, along with the effort everyone made to bring me here, means a lot to me," Casemiro said after signing for Inter Miami.

"I'm incredibly grateful, and I can't wait to get started so I can repay that trust, not only during the 90 minutes on matchday, but every day in training as well. All I can say is thank you, and I'll give everything I have to return the affection and confidence the club has shown me."

However, Sky Sports News understands United decided not to take up that option nor renew his contract and it was a decision made well before the end of the season.

The Red Devils have added Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans to their ranks this summer, and are believed to still be looking for a third midfielder.

Casemiro's Old Trafford career saw a resurgence over his last 18 months at the club, fighting his way back into the side having initially been unfavoured by former head coach Ruben Amorim. Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth contract amid strong interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, Sky Sports News understands.

United, Chelsea and Arsenal are believed to remain the frontrunners for Scott, who travelled to the United States with the England squad ahead of the World Cup, while other clubs are also keen.

Bournemouth expect Scott to remain their player this season whether he signs a new offer or continues on his current deal.

Sports.title: Antonelli among five drivers to miss Hungarian GP first practice
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will be among five drivers to sit out first practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix on Friday.

During the season, each Formula 1 team must run a rookie in at least two practice sessions for both of their cars and the familiarity of the Hungaroring, and it not being a Sprint weekend, means five teams have taken the opportunity to fulfil their obligation.

Antonelli, who leads Lewis Hamilton by 45 points and George Russell by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, will be replaced by Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti in Friday's first practice session.

Vesti drove Antonelli's car in first practice at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix last month, so the Italian will not miss any further practice sessions.

But, Russell has yet to hand his car over to a rookie so will miss two practice sessions during the 11 scheduled rounds following the summer break.

"I'm really excited to get back behind the wheel of the W17 and continue building my experience with the car. It's a great opportunity and one I'm looking forward to making the most of," said Vesti, who was the 2023 Formula 2 runner-up.

Image: Frederik Vesti is Mercedes' reserve driver (Memmler/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Images)

Which rookies will be running in Hungarian first practice? Mercedes - Frederik Vesti (Kimi Antonelli)

McLaren - Leonardo Fornaroli (Oscar Piastri)

Alpine - Paul Aron (Franco Colapinto)

Haas - Ryo Hirakawa (Oliver Bearman)

Cadillac - Colton Herta (Valtteri Bottas)

F2 champion Fornaroli replaces Piastri amid Haas rumours

Reigning Formula 2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli will make his second Friday outing of the season when he takes over Oscar Piastri's car at McLaren.

Fornaroli, who won the F3 and F2 titles in consecutive seasons in 2024 and 2025, drove Lando Norris' car in Barcelona last month and has been linked to a Haas seat for next year.

Also in June, McLaren loaned the 21-year-old Italian out to Haas for a TPC (Testing of Previous Cars) test amid speculation Fornaroli could join Haas full-time in 2027 to replace Esteban Ocon.

"At the moment we are not deciding anything. We're simply keeping the options open. We are not in a hurry, but Leo did a great job [in the test]," said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

Image: Leonardo Fornaroli celebrates winning the 2025 F2 title

Haas' Oliver Bearman will also miss first practice in Budapest as Ryo Hirakawa gets his second outing of the season, while Paul Aron will have his third of 2026 when he drives Franco Colapinto's Alpine.

Aron was previously loaned out to Audi earlier this year for practice sessions in Barcelona and Austria.

Former IndyCar star Colton Herta will also be in action in first practice as he gets behind the wheel of Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac.

Sports.title: Menzies withdraws from World Matchplay Darts after becoming unwell on stage
Sports.content:
Cameron Menzies' match against Ross Smith at the World Matchplay Darts was abandoned after the Scot became dizzy on stage and later fainted at the Winter Gardens on Wednesday night.

Menzies was 2-1 up in the second-round match when he doubled over in discomfort and appeared to become unsteady on his feet, with both Smith and the match officials coming to his aid.

The 37-year-old received medical attention after being taken from the stage, with the PDC later confirming Menzies had experienced high blood pressure. After medical checks, Menzies was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

The match was officially abandoned, with Smith progressing to the quarter-finals where he will face either Gerwyn Price or Rob Cross.

A statement from the PDC said: "Cameron Menzies was taken ill during his round two match against Ross Smith at the Betfred World Matchplay on Wednesday evening.

"Cameron experienced high blood pressure, which caused him to feel dizzy and subsequently faint.

"Following an assessment by the on-site medical team, Cameron was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

"We wish Cameron all the best and look forward to seeing him back in action soon."

Following a short break, Gian van Veen's match against Wessel Nijman commenced.

"I echo the thoughts of everybody; right now, it's all about Cameron Menzies," Sky Sports' Glen Durrant said.

"He's in tip-top form at the moment. It's a real tough one to take."

Image: Following assessments, medics said Menzies was 'sitting up, conscious and talking with his partner'

Menzies had advanced to the second round of the World Matchplay Darts after beating 2024 champion Luke Humphries 10-7, a victory he called "the biggest moment of my darts career."

The Scot produced a Big Fish checkout to beat the world No 2, and afterwards, was left lost for words.

"I don't know how to explain that [victory]. I did believe in my heart that I could maybe cause an upset but I would have to play it out of my skin," Menzies said.

"I wouldn't say I played it out of my skin, but I played really well. I did say before the game started, to beat Luke, I need to take every chance that he gives me.

"It's not like Luke to give a lot of chances away, but obviously I'm going to take it. A lot went in. I was happy. I stole a few legs to win, but it's made the best moment of my darts career."

Sports.title: 'Silly Bodybuilder', 'Mr Greedy Belly' - AJ and Fury clash as doubts cast over fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have traded insults as fresh doubts were raised about their long-awaited showdown this year.

Fury returns against Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday before Joshua has a comeback fight against Kristian Prenga on Saturday in Saudi Arabia.

The British rivals were expected to finally face each other in November, with a date and venue yet to be announced, but Fury insists he is prepared to fight "somebody else" later this year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua hit back at Fury's comments by branding his British rival 'Mr Greedy Belly'

However, speaking to Dev Sahni on Sky Sports News, Fury cast doubt on the fight with Joshua in an expletive rant about his compatriot.

"Let's not make this about silly Mr Bodybuilder. I'm not interested in him or his mates or anybody else. I don't give a **** about him. I don't care if I ever see him again in my life. If I do, I do. If I don't, I don't," he said.

"I'm not interested in him, anybody should do for him - his manager, his wife, his sister, his cousin. No interest.

"We have got five months left of the year, so I want to get this fella [Wach] boxed, do well, and do what I can.

"I know I can beat this fella. I beat this fella with one hand, and that's not to say anything bad about Mariusz, but I'm in good form. I could beat all of these heavyweights with one hand. But I'm in good shape. I'm in fine fettle, injury-free and I'm ready to rock and roll.

"There's five months to get another fight in before the end of year. And if it is your man Anthony Joshua, good. And if it's not, then I'll be fighting somebody else."

Joshua later hit back at Fury, branding his British rival as "Mr Greedy Belly" and insisting he would "do his part of the bargain, by beating Prenga this weekend".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Jones discusses the best iterations of former world champions Fury and Joshua

"He's always been talking about my body for so many years," Joshua said. "What I would do for him at a discounted rate because of his profile, I'll help him transform his body from being a greedy belly into a bodybuilder. I'll give him a set of six-pack abs.

"I'll give him a set of abs. If he's really keen to know what it takes to look like this, I'll help him out. He's always obsessed with my abs.

"It's going down. If I get past my next fight, I've stood up, I've done my part of the bargain. And now it's up to your mate, Mr Greedy Belly, to fulfil his obligation to get in the ring with me."

Could Fury vs AJ happen 2am?

Wembley Stadium might have to extend its current curfew time to 2am to accommodate an international TV broadcast and Joshua is open to a later fight time.

"Quick party, quick central London, local Wetherspoons or whatever it is, and then hit the fight night in Wembley. That would be unbelievable," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn backs Joshua to beat Fury if the British rivals finally meet later this year, insisting Wembley Stadium is the ideal venue for fans

Fury has no plans to watch Joshua's fight

Fury's fight with Wach on Friday will take place at around 4pm UK time in front of 1,500 spectators in Pattaya, with Joshua fighting on Saturday night in Jeddah.

Joshua attended Fury's victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov in April earlier this year in London but Fury will not travel to Saudi Arabia.

"I'm going home. I've got about as much interest in Anthony Joshua versus 'some Pringles' as I have of spewing that all over the floor. None. I'm going home. I'm not interested in AJ and his mate boxing," he said.

Asked if facing off against Joshua in Saudi Arabia on Saturday would send a signal to everyone that the fight is happening, Fury added: "You can send out as many signals as you want.

"You've been told for 10 years it's happening. It hasn't happened, has it? So don't hold your breath. I've always had my doubts. But if it happens, good. If it doesn't, also good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Turki Al-Sheikh provides an update on where Fury vs Joshua could take place. Credit: SELA.

Fury: Wach is a tough man

Wach was last a heavyweight world champion in 2012 but has continued to fight annually, although has lost eight of his last 12 fights.

The 46-year-old wants to "ruin" the plans of Fury fighting Joshua, and Fury is not overlooking his opponent.

"It's going to be crazy but I'm looking forward to the challenge. It's going to be good," said 'The Gypsy King'.

"He's a tough man. He's a veteran, and he's been around the game 20 years plus. So he's a dangerous man, a big heavyweight and anything can happen. I've got to obviously be wary of him and be on my A-game and do what I do.

"I've been out here 10 weeks training, so I've not left any stones unturned. I'm ready to go. I'm in great shape and I'm fit as a fiddle."

Sports.title: Is Barcola next on Arsenal's list after missing out on Rogers?
Sports.content:
Arsenal retain an interest in Bradley Barcola after missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea, according to Sky Sports News reporter Dharmesh Sheth.

The Gunners are looking at alternative options to bolster their attack after their top transfer target Rogers joined Chelsea from Aston Villa in £117m deal - which is a new record for a British player.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this summer that Paris Saint-Germain could allow Barcola to leave if the right offer comes in.
