View image in fullscreen Phil Foden says he is hoping his game can reach another level with Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Manchester City

Last season, after the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on 4 March, Foden started two league games and was substituted after 58 minutes of the 2-1 FA Cup final victory over Southampton. Foden has spent his whole career with City, joining as an eight-year-old.

Viana said: “Everyone at ­Manchester City is incredibly proud of Phil. He represents everything good about our academy. He is a unique ­talent and his creativity is a joy to watch. None of what he has achieved would be possible without the focus, dedication and humility to work hard in every moment and absorb all of the knowledge available to him through our coaches and players.

“At 26, his development is still ongoing, and we look forward to ­seeing the player Phil can become over the coming years.”

After the 2025 FA Cup 1-0 final defeat by Crystal Palace, Foden revealed he had been struggling with off-field problems. He had also played with pain after suffering an ankle problem sustained from a Casemiro tackle in a goalless draw at ­Manchester United in April.

Sports.title: More chaos at Southampton! Spying Saints boss Tonda Eckert is facing lengthy ban after being hit with fresh charges for THREE breaches by the FA after play-off scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton manager Tonda Eckert is facing a lengthy FA ban after being charged with three counts of spying on opposition training.

Daily Mail Sport expect Eckert, who has seven days to respond, not to contest the charge after accepting culpability while openly cooperating with the FA's thorough interview process.

It comes after Southampton were expelled from the Championship play-offs and slapped with a four-point deduction for the 2026-27 season by the EFL when Daily Mail Sport revealed an intern analyst was spotted observing Middlesbrough training on the eve of their play-off semi-final clash in May.

The EFL's probe revealed two further instances of spying, authorised by Eckert, last season.

Southampton sources believe they have already faced sufficient punishment and would deem any potential sporting sanction by the FA excessive - given the penalty from the EFL, which Saints have urged the FA to consider.

They are also hopeful that Eckert's compliance with the investigation will earn favour with the disciplinary commission and avoid a ban.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA with three breaches of misconduct following the Spygate scandal

The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-off final in May following the saga

That said, should the FA opt for a ban, sources with knowledge of the situation suggest Eckert could be prevented from managing in England for up to two years.

If the FA decide on a less severe punishment, a fine would be imposed. Saints hope any sanction will be a suspended touchline ban at worst.

There is very little precedent for the case. Leeds United manager Marcelo Bielsa was not charged by the FA when he admitted to sending a member of staff to spy on Derby County's training in January 2019. The EFL, however, imposed a £200,000 fine - which Bielsa personally paid.

FIFA banned Canada women's head coach Bev Priestman from football for 12 months when she authorised surveillance of New Zealand's training during the 2024 Paris Olympics. This, though, involved a drone.

Despite the absence of similar cases in England, Rule E.3.1 - which Eckert has been charged with - is extremely broad and encompasses misconduct from bad language to bringing the game into disrepute.

For example, Burnley's Hannibal Mejbri was given a four-match ban last season for spitting at Leeds United fans. While vastly dissimilar incidents, both cases breach the same rule.

Eckert is carrying out his responsibilities as usual at Southampton and focused on preparations for the new season, with the first team set to travel to Germany for pre-season training. Southampton insist Eckert maintains their full support.

Acknowledging the charge, Saints said: 'Southampton Football Club and First Team Head Coach Tonda Eckert acknowledge today's charges from The FA relating to a breach of Rule E3.1.

'Tonda and the club will continue to cooperate fully and openly with The FA.

A Southampton analyst was caught watching Middlesbrough's training session ahead of the play-off semi final

'Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026/27 Championship season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.'

In a recent interview with Sky Sports, Eckert said: 'It's been an emotional summer. I can't lie, obviously, when the news broke towards the back end of last season, it's tough.

'It's not easy in that very moment. It's not easy to look into the eyes of the players. They're just so disappointed, and so many emotions coming out.

'You get so many threats at one point. You have police protection at one point; you can't drive a car. It's tough to deal with that for the very moment.

'When things calmed down with time, and I went back home, different challenges at home, you have a moment to reflect.

'I think that over the months there's also been a lot of positives that we can take into next season.

'After a couple of weeks, that excitement comes back in to go again and show what we are about.'

Eckert and Southampton came under significant scrutiny surrounding the whole incident and were heavily criticised for their poor communication and lack of accountability when the news broke.

Things later intensified when the written reasons for the punishment were released, with several damning revelations about the involvement of Eckert in the spying operation.

Leaked WhatsApp messages revealed the German showing his 'love' of the cheating, with one explaining how Salt was told, 'You legend. Manager loved it' after a spying mission on Oxford United in December.

Southampton's attempts to cover up their cheating were similarly eye-watering.

Despite the pressure, Saints owner Dragan Solak opted to stick with Eckert rather than sack him, with the German coach addressing fans in a video statement in June.

Eckert, speaking in full for the first time since the ruling, hardly blinked in the lengthy video, saying: 'Hi, Saints supporters. What I'm going to say is not going to be perfect, but I will try to be as honest and clear as I can be.

'I think you deserve that. For everything that's happened, I do want to apologise, and I hold my hand up because as a head coach, I am responsible.

'I am responsible for everything that has happened in this football club. I am responsible for everything that has happened in my coaching staff.

Eckert, who could be banned from football, publicly apologised to Saints supporters in June

Southampton owner Dragan Solak threw his backing behind Eckert despite the scandal

'I do apologise to the supporters, to everyone who has travelled with us, who has supported us over so many games.'

In the clip entitled: 'A personal message from Tonda Eckert', he went on: 'To the ones who have shared emotions game by game, who have managed to bring us all the way up to this very end of the season.

'We were supposed to play the biggest game of the season. I apologise to the players, who have done absolutely everything that they can. They have done absolutely everything in the last six months to bring this club back to where it belongs. They would have deserved to play the final.'

He added: 'They would have deserved to play the final with you, just like they've done two years ago, and just like they've done in the semi-final against Man City.

'It hurts to see the employees of the club, it hurts to see the staff, it hurts to see the players who have invested so much in the preparation for games.

'Those who have invested so much to leave their families at home to recover and to prepare for the games coming up, who had hurt so much.

'To see their pain on the day the decision came in, because it has such a big impact, not just on them and their career, but also on their families. I apologise to all of the clubs that have been involved, and mostly I apologise to our supporters.'

Eckert then went on to 'give context' to the spying, arguing that his experiences in different leagues have coloured his thinking.

He explained: 'When I worked in Italy for over four years, every starting line-up that we've chosen for the games was always out in the media before games.

'The reason is that our training sessions, especially the ones before games, have always been observed by the media and have always been observed by opponent teams that we came up against.

'[Pep] Guardiola has spoken about this at his time at Bayern Munich, that it has been common practice in Germany to observe training sessions, knowing that other teams would do the same.

'I don't want to say this to excuse anything that we have done. I just want to give you context in the way that I grew up in the football world.

'There are different rules in England. There are different rules from the EFL. And I should have known them.'

He later added: 'I am a young coach. I have made a mistake, and I take full responsibility. I want to thank Dragan and the board for the support, especially in times like this.

'With everything that I have said, without script and without a predefined statement. Speaking to you from the heart, I hope that you have an overview of what has happened over the last weeks.

'I hope that over time you can understand and forgive, and I hope to see you all soon.'

Sports.title: Only ONE England player makes FIFA's 2026 World Cup team of the tournament as fans choose Man United star in defence - and cult hero gets the nod
Sports.content:
FIFA have only selected one England player in their World Cup team of the tournament.

After six weeks of action in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, in which Spain ended up adding a second star to their crest after beating Argentina at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, the football governing body has announced their ‘Dream XI’.

The team of the tournament is selected based on votes from the fans, and only Jude Bellingham managed to sneak into the side from the Three Lions squad.

The 23-year-old midfielder netted seven goals, the most-ever by an England player in a single World Cup, as the Three Lions secured their best placing at the tournament since the triumph in 1966 by beating France 6-4 in the third-place play-off.

The majority of the team was completed by the fellow semi-finalists as three spots in the team were filled by Spain players, with three more from France, and two from the former champions Argentina.

Bellingham is joined by Rodri, who lifted the World Cup trophy aloft as Spain captain, and Michael Olise.

Jude Bellingham was the only England player voted to be in the World Cup 'Dream XI'

40-year-old Vozinha was selected in goal after earning cult hero status for his role in Cape Verde's run to the round of 32

The Spanish midfielder was back to his best at this tournament, and his performances in the spine of the champions' side earned him the Golden Ball. Meanwhile, Olise secured the record for the most assists at a single World Cup with seven.

In front of them, the new all-time World Cup record goalscorer Kylian Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot, occupies the right wing, while the man he overtook in his final game of the tournament, Lionel Messi, is on the left.

Messi was the first to break the scoring record, netting five goals in his first two games of the tournament to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals.

However, the goals dried up after the round of 16 stage, and he has likely finished his World Cup career with an astonishing 20 goals.

In between them is Norway's Erling Haaland, who spearheaded his country to a first-ever quarter-final by scoring seven goals in his first appearance at the competition.

The back four contained Spanish full-backs Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, while France's Dayot Upamecano and Argentina's Lisandro Martinez were selected in the heart of defence.

And at the base of the team, in between the sticks, was none other than Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha.

The 40-year-old was one of the heroes of his country's remarkable run to the last-32 stage before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

The shot-stopper also hit the headlines for gaining an outrageous amount of Instagram followers throughout the World Cup.

At the start of Cape Verde's World Cup opener with Spain, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram. But after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 29.5million followers.

Sports.title: Aston Villa agree Alejandro Garnacho deal: Ex-Man United star leaves Chelsea on loan with conditional obligation to buy
Sports.content:
Aston Villa agree Alejandro Garnacho deal: Ex-Man United star leaves Chelsea on loan with conditional obligation to buy

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

The 22-year-old has been convinced by Unai Emery and joins on loan with a conditional obligation to buy. Sources say the conditions are easily achievable and the total package meets the Blues' initial £43million valuation of the player.

The Argentina international has travelled to Birmingham today to complete his medical and will sign a four-year contract once the move becomes permanent.

Manchester United are due a sell-on percentage.

Aston Villa had made enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m move to Chelsea.

Alejandro Garnacho has left Chelsea to join Aston Villa on loan with a conditional obligation

Roma had also offered a loan with options for Garnacho.

Garnacho had previously been of interest to Villa before he left Man United last summer.

The Argentine winger played 43 matches for Chelsea last season in all competitions.

Garnacho featured 24 times in the Premier League for the Blues, scoring one goal and providing three assists.

He scored eight times in total for Chelsea, with half of his goals coming in the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer briefing: Why the Bruno Guimaraes deal could be hijacked, blow in Bradley Barcola chase, La Liga stars on radar, latest on Bournemouth duo and major William Saliba injury update
Sports.content:
Arsenal are effectively being told 'to put up or shut up' in their pursuit of Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

All discussions so far have come from the Brazilian midfielder's agent and Newcastle are becoming increasingly agitated by what they view as a 'tactical process' with the player becoming distracted by the speculation over his future which is being played out in public.

Guimaraes has told Newcastle he wishes to talk to Arsenal and have the chance to win more titles but the club stance is he is not for sale.

Arsenal have been led to believe a deal for the 28-year-old can be achieved for around £75million but Newcastle would need more than that to be persuaded. They have had no formal offers from the Premier League champions and would point to the increasing market rate for midfielders.

The onus is firmly on sporting director Andrea Berta coming to the table with a proper offer.

Arsenal have been led to believe a deal for the 28-year-old Bruno Guimaraes can be achieved for around £75million but Newcastle would need more than that to be persuaded

How did Arsenal miss out on Rogers?

And there are other Premier League clubs circling around Guimaraes. That will sound all too familiar to Arsenal fans. It will stick in the craw to see Morgan Rogers declaring his delight at joining 'London's biggest club' ... Chelsea.

For a long period, Arsenal thought they were in pole position for Rogers, but they were led to believe £80m to £100m would be enough. Villa felt they weren't reading the market.

That became more apparent when Villa co-owner and chairman Nassef Sawiris had an informal chat with Arsenal in the USA and it was clear they were some distance apart in terms of their prices. Arsenal had their valuation in mind, despite Villa insisting on a record fee for a British player.

Arsenal were favourites for Rogers. As Daily Mail Sport reported, England team-mates Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka were part of a charm offensive. Martin Odegaard also spoke to Rogers, as did manager Mikel Arteta.

The 23-year-old was open to the move, even though a little typecast as a replacement for Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, who is also for sale, as an option for the left wing. It just needed the right bid.

Yet when Arsenal failed to read the room, Chelsea seized their chance. The Blues began formal negotiations with Villa and Rogers’ representatives the day after England’s semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Reece James leaned on Rogers, Cole Palmer sent his best pal a text message and Arteta's old childhood friend, Xabi Alonso, phoned Rogers on Friday to explain his plans. Personal terms were agreed the same day. Chelsea agreed on £117m and Arsenal were informed. They decided their money could be spent better elsewhere.

Arsenal put on a charm offensive for Morgan Rogers (above) with Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard all speaking to the player - but he ended up at Chelsea

Reece James (right) helped convince Rogers to move to Stamford Bridge

Now Rogers has gone, who are Arsenal after?

Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez remains a dream target. Though he is set on Barcelona, Arsenal would bid if they thought they had a chance.

Arsenal are also competing with Liverpool for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola though the Anfield club are considered to have the upper hand at this stage.

Spain World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been suggested again as he considers leaving Barcelona, with PSG favourites. There are also rumblings Nico Williams could finally consider leaving Athletic Bilbao once he finishes his holiday.

'We need to stay calm; let him enjoy himself and disconnect from soccer. What is meant to happen will happen,' said his agent Felix Tainta helpfully.

All have been discussed. But the price has to be right.

The same applies to £85m-rated Eli Junior Kroupi at Bournemouth and his team-mate Alex Scott. Arsenal know from Chelsea's failed bid that it will take more than £64m to prise away the 22-year-old midfielder Scott this summer.

Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi is now £85m when he was considered a £60m prospect before the World Cup. Manchester City are leading that chase.

Roma's Manu Kone is another Arsenal are briefed on. He would be more affordable if they proceed, though Manchester United are also around that deal.

Arsenal did make an exploratory call to RB Leipzig over Yan Diomande's situation in recent days but he is still expected to join PSG.

Liverpool are ahead of Arsenal in the race for PSG and France star Bradley Barcola

Arsenal are keen on midfielder Alex Scott but know it is going to take a lot of money to get him out of Bournemouth

And the defence?

William Saliba has decided not to have surgery on his back injury after consultation with Arsenal. But the player will have a long period of rest. The duration is still to be determined, but is likely to be three to four months – so it is crucial they find suitable cover.

Free agent John Stones, another Chelsea and Inter Milan target, is on their list, as is West Ham's versatile Aaron Wan-Bissaka – but not at £25m.

Maxence Lacroix was a player discussed briefly but is destined for Chelsea and Inter are reluctant to lose Jacobo Ramon.

Arsenal's recent enquiry for Villa defender Ezri Konsa showed the clubs were miles apart. The Gunners value the England centre back at around £30-35m, Villa see it more like £60m. Konsa would like to join Arsenal but they know Villa's stance.

Real Madrid's Raul Asencio, now surplus at the Bernabeu, is another name to be floated.

In good news, at least Ben White is fit again and in no rush to depart. And as Daily Mail Sport revealed, Arsenal have also added highly-rated centre back Elijah Upson from neighbours Tottenham. Though compensation has still to be agreed for the 18-year-old son of former England defender Matthew, he could push himself into the first-team scene quickly.

Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix was discussed by Arsenal briefly but he is destined for Chelsea

Arsenal and Aston Villa have very different ideas about the value of Ezri Konsa (right)

Any youngsters in Arsenal's sights?

Despite the disappointment of missing out to Manchester City in the race for 17-year-old winger Jeremy Monga, Arsenal are pushing to sign 16-year-old Crystal Palace striker Mylo Bernard. His contract expired last month, however, Palace have also offered improved terms.

Arsenal have spoken to Cardiff City too about Axel Donczew. The 16-year-old midfielder became the youngest player in Cardiff's history last season.

And who's heading for the exit?

Fulham have rekindled interest in winger Reiss Nelson, who needs to find regular game time after a disappointing loan at Brentford. Benfica and Valencia are also in the mix.

Charles Sagoe Jr is wanted by AIK in Sweden and Hamburg continue to try and appease Arsenal with offers for Fabio Vieira.

Eric Huwer, Hamburg's chief financial officer, told German media yesterday: 'We fell a bit in love with Fabio Vieira last year. We feel like we’re fighting for him every single day. We’ve also backed up our interest with Arsenal with financial figures, but right now, no one is flinching.

'We’re confident we can make Fabio a very competitive offer within our means. We’re naturally very curious to see whether he and Arsenal will accept it.'

Indeed.

Sports.title: Darts star has to be helped off stage after suffering health scare during World Matchplay clash as he's forced to withdraw from tournament
Sports.content:
Darts star Cameron Menzies was helped off stage after falling unwell during the World Matchplay Darts.

Menzies had been leading Ross Smith in his second round match when he appeared to sway and look faint on stage.

He was seen speaking to a tournament official and bent over, before being helped off by Smith.

'We are having a break in our first match because Cameron Menzies is unwell,' presenter Emma Paton told Sky Sports viewers.

'All we know at the moment is that he is being seen to by St John's Ambulance.

'He is with some medics at the moment. Hopefully he is ok and feeling better very shortly.'

Darts star Cameron Menzies was helped off stage after falling unwell during the World Matchplay Darts

Menzies received treatment after suffering from high blood pressure and was deemed well enough to return to his accomodation

The darts star had been forced to withdraw from his second round match at the tournament

PDC statement: Cameron Menzies pic.twitter.com/tPBaeNPSa0 — PDC Darts (@OfficialPDC) July 22, 2026

The PDC later confirmed that Menzies had been forced to withdraw through illness.

'Cameron Menzies is unable to continue his Round Two clash after being taken unwell,' a PDC statement read.

'Ross Smith progresses to the Quarter-Finals as a result.

'The next match between Gian van Veen and Wessel Nijman will start shortly.'

The PDC issued a subsequent update confirming Menzies had been suffering from 'high blood pressure' but after assessment was deemed well enough to return to his accomodation.

'Cameron Menzies was taken ill during his round two match against Ross Smith at the Betfred World Matchplay on Wednesday evening,' the statement read.

'Cameron experienced high blood pressure, which caused him to feel dizzy and subsequently faint.

'Following an assessment by the on-site medical team, Cameron was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

'We wish Cameron all the best and look forward to seeing him back in action soon.'

Sports.title: Spurs fans fume at missing £85m new star Mateus Fernandes' wondergoal on 'pure garbage' in-house channel's coverage of pre-season friendly
Sports.content:
Tottenham fans have expressed their frustration after being unable to watch £85million signing Mateus Fernandes' superb goal in pre-season amid technical problems with the club's in-house TV channel.

Fans wanting to watch Tottenham's first pre-season match against MK Dons needed to tune in to their channel SPURSPLAY, which is carrying all of the club's pre-season matches.

The subscription is a benefit this season for the club's One Hotspur+ Members, while fans alternatively can pay £45 for an annual subscription or £35 if they are a One Hotspur member.

Fans had been looking to catch a first glimpse of their new midfield partnership of Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, who joined for £100m from Newcastle.

Fernandes opened the scoring just three minutes into the match, superbly volleying into the top corner from outside the box after MK Dons' goalkeeper had punched clear.

Tottenham's official X account shared the goal while highlighting that fans could watch on SPURSPLAY, prompting replies from fans already struggling with the service.

Tottenham fans were angered after missing £85m signing Mateus Fernandes' stunning goal in their opening pre-season match due to issues with the club's in-house channel

What a hit, Mateus Fernandes 💥



Watch our pre-season games live on SPURSPLAY! — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) July 22, 2026

Fernandes opened the scoring in Tottenham's pre-season match clash against MK Dons with a stunning volley from the edge of the area

'We can’t,' one fan responded while sharing a screenshot of the website that stated 'We are sorry, an error occurred. Please retry in a few minutes.'

'It seems this application has become very popular, and its available rate limit has been reached. Please retry in a few minutes,' an error message read.

One fan responded: 'This stream is running like pure garbage. If this doesn’t improve I will be demanding a refund.'

'I’d love to, but you won’t let me even though I paid my hard earned money. Well done,' a second added.

Another posted: 'Managing to get 10-15 secs then freezes. Every time. Were Spurs really not expecting massive interest considering they include Spursplay in the plus membership??,'

'How is it every season you fail to account for how many people might want to login and watch the friendlies. Seriously EVERY YEAR,' one fan said.

'Why is Spursplay stream not working? Only get still frames, anyone else had the same issue?' another added.

The friendly at Tottenham's Hotspur Way training centre is the club's first of their pre-season schedule.

Roberto De Zerbi's side will then travel to New Zealand to face Auckland FC on July 26, before taking on Sydney FC and Chelsea in matches on July 29 and August 1 in Sydney.

Tottenham then face Getafe and have two matches against Hoffenheim before beginning their Premier League season with a trip to Brentford on August 22.

Sports.title: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal - as Issa Diop makes £8.5m Premier League switch: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Roma's Summerville hijack plot fails

West Ham's Crysencio Summerville has accepted Al-Hilal's proposal.

Roma had made a last ditch effort to persuade the 24-year-old to join them but were told by West Ham they would have to increase their offer after Al-Hilal had a bid of £55m plus £5m in add ons accepted on Tuesday.

Garnacho heading to Villa

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho on loan from Chelsea

The 22-year-old has been convinced by Unai Emery and joins on a loan with a conditional obligation to buy.

The Argentina international has travelled to Birmingham today to complete his medic and will sign a four year contract once the move becomes permanent.

Manchester United are due a sell on percentage.

Hull pushing to beat Ipswich for free agent Morita

Hull City have moved to try and beat Ipswich Town to the signing of Hidemasa Morita following his departure from Sporting Lisbon as a free agent.

Leeds United had also been in talks with the 31-year-old prior to the midfielder leaving the Portuguese side this summer.

Morita was a popular figure at Sporting, he played 31 times last season, and fans wanted him to stay but he now looks increasingly likely to join Premier League new boys Hull after their ambitious play to sign him.

Roma's last-gasp Summerville swoop

Roma have made a last-ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to choose them over Al-Hilal.

Coach Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Summerville last night to try and convince him Roma's project was more suitable for the Netherlands international.

Al Hilal have agreed a £60m fee with West Ham with £55m up front.

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to sign for them

Roma had offered £39m plus add ons.

The Italians are also keen on Chelsea defender Axel Disasi who was a teammate of Summerville's at West Ham last season.

They also made an offer for Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho but Aston Villa's proposal for the winger offers more guarantees.

Wober departs Elland Road

Leeds United defender Maximilian Wober is joining Schalke on a free transfer.

The 28-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen, has been having a medical with Schalke.

Wober and Leeds are finalising a mutual agreement to terminate his contract a year early.

Valencia remain keen to sign Leeds attacking midfielder Largie Ramazani too.

Van Hecke completes Spurs move

Fellow Netherlands international Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton.

The Dutch centre-half, who chalked up three goals and three assists from 36 Premier League match for the Seagulls last term, had one year left on his contract at the Amex before Spurs swooped in to sign him.

It marks the latest signing in what has been a busy transfer window for Spurs, with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Andrew Robertson, Martin Dubravka and Marcos Senesi all joining Roberto De Zerbi's ranks ahead of the new season.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough have confirmed the signing of striker Will Lankshear from Tottenham in a deal worth £20million including add-ons.

He has signed a five year contract and said: 'Middlesbrough is such a massive club over the years; I deem it to be a Premier League club.

'The project here really excites me. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the journey, and get this club back where it belongs.'

Lankshear scored 11 goals in 43 appearances for Oxford United last season and also had interest from Wolves.

Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton

Tigers see £13.6m Danois bid rejected

Hull City have had a £13.6million bid rejected for Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old, who is also on Newcastle United’s watchlist, has emerged as a top target for Hull but Auxerre value him closer to £25million.

That would require Hull to smash their club transfer record and they want at least two new midfielders.

Danois is a France U21 international and made 33 appearances in Ligue 1 last term, scoring three times and registering one assist.

Liverpool's swoop for Monaco star comes up short

Liverpool made an approach for Monaco attacking midfielder Maghnes Akliouche early in the window.

The club checked on the potential availability of the 24-year-old but it was evident he was a prime target for Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG have made offers to Monaco for the France international but have still to agree on the fee.

Liverpool did not progress with talks after their initial check and are exploring other options including PSG's Bradley Barcola.

Wolves outcast Arokodare poised for swift exit

Ajax have joined the clubs showing interest in Wolves' wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare.

Arokodare will not be part of Wolves' squad to face Maidenhead tonight after his actions prompted coach Cesar Peixoto to cancel training on Monday.

The Nigerian refused to exit the training pitch when asked prompting the session to be cancelled. Extra security was then called in to the training ground on Tuesday to ensure the 25-year-old striker did not disrupt the session again.

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry.

Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

In April, he faced disciplinary action after a dressing room bust-up with team-mate Mateus Mane during a 4-0 defeat at West Ham.

Wolves cancelled training after wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch

Diop makes Premier League switch

Ipswich Town have confirmed the signing of Issa Diop from Fulham in a deal worth around £8.5m.

The centre-back has signed a four-year deal.

Ipswich schedule medical

Ipswich have also scheduled a medical for this week ahead of completing the £10million signing of Daizen Maeda from Celtic.

Ipswich agreed a deal for the forward worth an initial £8m plus £2m in add-ons.

Talks are continuing over a deal for free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita, formerly of Sporting Lisbon, as well as Union SG’s Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

Sports.title: Revealed: Rodri is pushing to sign for Real Madrid - and move from Man City could spark a midfield merry-go-round involving Man United target
Sports.content:
Manchester City midfielder Rodri is waiting for Real Madrid president Florentino Perez to give the green light for his proposed return to Spain.

City have already signed Elliot Anderson and are working on a deal for Lille midfield prodigy Ayyoub Bouaddi, mindful that Rodri and his representatives have still to accept terms on the new contract they offered in April.

The 30-year-old, who has one year left on his City deal, is keen on a return to Madrid and there is growing support for the move on the back of him leading Spain to World Cup glory.

Perez was initially reluctant to back the transfer but others within the club have suggested it would be a good deal for the club and their image.

Jose Mourinho has been brought in to eradicate a perceived divisiveness in the Madrid dressing room and has already pushed for senior players to be recruited.

But the consequences could mean others departing.

Rodri is waiting for Real Madrid president Florentino Perez to give the green light to his return to Spain

Manchester United have not made fresh enquiries about Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni

Aurelien Tchouameni has agreed a new contract extension and wants to stay in Madrid but could find opportunities become limited. Likewise, as Daily Mail Sport reported, his France compatriot Eduardo Camavinga could also yet depart.

As a result, Premier League clubs are attentive to the situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while Manchester United have a long-held interest in Tchouameni, they have not made fresh enquiries since their initial contacts months ago and established that the 26-year-old would also be very expensive and difficult to place in their current wage structure.

Camavinga has been considered by City, Chelsea and Arsenal. Despite his experience, he is still only 23. He could represent greater value but key is whether either would leave Madrid.

Other players expected to go are Gonzalo Garcia who is wanted by Fulham and Franco Mastantuono who will be allowed out on loan. Raul Asencio will also go as they work to recoup funds for Rodri and one more showpiece signing.

Sports.title: Cameron Menzies urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident
Sports.content:
Cameron Menzies urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident

Action at the World Matchplay had to be suspended during Cameron Menzies' clash with Ross Smith as the former was taken off stage to receive medical attention - later withdrawing

View 2 Images Cameron Menzies was helped off the stage during his match with Ross Smith

Play at the World Matchplay in Blackpool had to be halted after Cameron Menzies was forced to leave the stage to receive medical attention - leading to his withdrawal from the tournament.

‌



He was leading Ross Smith 2-1 but the fourth leg of their contest was put on hold. Before Menzies slumped over he was swaying on the stage, which caught the attention of those around him. He looked as if he was feeling faint before his discomfort became obvious.

‌



Sky Sports presenter Emma Paton stated that Menzies was still being assessed and was conscious. He was able to sit up and was able to talk to his partner.

‌



After his withdrawal was confirmed, the PDC confirmed Menzies had been cleared to return to his accommodation, with a high blood pressure presented as the reason for his dizziness.

The PDC statement reads: "Cameron Menzies was taken ill during his round two match against Ross Smith at the Betfred World Matchplay on Wednesday evening.

Darts star puts CV on job site Indeed after dismal year and wild punching incident READ MORE :

Luke Litter takes huge six-figure financial hit immediately after Premier League Darts win READ MORE :

"Cameron experienced high blood pressure, which caused him to feel dizzy and subsequently faint. Following an assessment by the on-site medical team, Cameron was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

‌



"We wish Cameron all the best and look forward to seeing him back in action soon."

Mark Webster added on the incident: "Smith was obviously concerned. He'll be offering his support. While the medics are seeing to Cameron, he's got to stay on the practice board. But ultimately it's just about hoping that Cameron is okay at the minute."

View 2 Images Cameron Menzies has been forced to withdraw from the tournament

‌



Smith has ultimately progressed to the quarter-finals as a result of Menzies' unfortunate illness. After Menzies' withdrawal the night's second match - Gian van Veen vs Wessel Nijman - was bought forward.

Paton later added on the situation: "He has been cleared by medics. He is okay, but he will play no further part in tonight's action."

Menzies had never made it past the first round of this tournament, but made it through after a brilliant win over Luke Humphries in the previous round.

Article continues below

And he was leading early against Smith, making his withdrawal all the more challenging. "I echo the thoughts of everybody; right now, it's all about Cameron Menzies," said Glen Durrant. "He's in tip top form at the moment. It's a real tough one to take."

Sports.title: Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot
Sports.content:
Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot

Benvenuto Cellini is the 11-4 second favourite for the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Ascot on Saturday, with trainer Aidan O'Brien drawing comparisons to his legendary grandfather Galileo

View 3 Images (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

Aidan O'Brien has drawn a comparison between Benvenuto Cellini and the colt's legendary grandfather Galileo, possessing all the same class and courage but "probably" a touch more pace, as he chases a first King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes triumph since 2016.

‌



The three year old is looking to build on his Irish Derby victory with a winning display at Ascot this weekend, a race Galileo himself won during his Classic year back in 2001.

‌



And while it represents the sternest examination of his career against a stellar line-up of older rivals, O'Brien is convinced the son of Frankel has every attribute needed to become only the seventh three year old winner of the race this century.

‌



Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone retired after finishing career on a high READ MORE :

"We think he's a very high-quality, classy horse on fast ground. He's probably a bit quicker than Galileo was, but he moves like him and we think he's brave like he was too," he said.

"There's no better mile-and-a-half race anywhere. It's a difficult race, usually run on fast ground and it's run at Ascot too, which is a very special place. You need a horse that stays.

"They have to have class and it's where the three-year-olds meet the older horses for the first time (at the trip)."

‌



Benvenuto Cellini will need to get the better of not only race favourite Calandagan but last year's runner-up Kalpana, Japanese star Masquerade Ball and stablemate and Arc runner-up Minnie Hauk, to name just four of what could be a field of ten.

View 3 Images Galileo (left) with jockey Michael Kinane wins the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes from Fantastic Light and jockey Frankie Dettori at Ascot today, Saturday 28th July 2001. **EDI** PA Photo : Tim Ockenden

O'Brien acknowledges he is unleashing two genuine contenders as he attempts to secure a prize he has claimed four times previously, with Dylan Thomas (2007), Duke Of Marmalade (2008) and Highland Reel (2016) joining Galileo's triumph.

‌



Minnie Hauk produced an excellent second behind Ombudsman in the Prince of Wales's Stakes last time out, a performance O'Brien believes will have set her up perfectly for the step back up to 12 furlongs.

"We ran her in the Prince of Wales's Stakes with a view to coming back for the King George, and we thought that was probably her best run ever. The extra couple of furlongs should really suit her," the trainer said.

Following her runner-up finish behind Daryz in Paris last October, Minnie Hauk concluded her campaign with a sixth-place effort behind Ethical Diamond in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Del Mar in California.

‌



View 3 Images Minnie Hauk has been backed to run well in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

Both the filly and Benvenuto Cellini could share the same objective, with the King George guaranteeing entry into the field for the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland at the end of October as part of the Breeders' Cup 'Win and You're In' series.

O'Brien explained: "The Breeders' Cup is massive. We went there last year (with Minnie Hauk) and got things wrong tactically. You can't go anywhere better, it's where all the horses meet. It's very competitive racing at good tracks and the atmosphere is second to none.

Article continues below

"Benvenuto Cellini could go too. He's a horse that will enjoy travelling and he's a great mover. He would be fine coming back to a mile and a quarter, and I think you need that kind of pace at the Breeders' Cup.

"He's an easy horse to train who doesn't take a lot of work so it could suit him perfectly."

Sports.title: From beach cleaning to the Commonwealth Games: Artist hopes King's baton raises awareness of threat of ocean plastic
Sports.content:
From beach cleaning to the Commonwealth Games: Artist hopes King's baton raises awareness of threat of ocean plastic

A King's Baton made from discarded plastic will carry a powerful environmental message into this week's opening ceremony in Glasgow.

View 2 Images Cornish artist Bonnie Steward designed Team England's King's baton for the Commonwealth Games.

From beach rubbish to centre stage at the Commonwealth Games.

‌



A King's Baton made from discarded plastic will carry a powerful environmental message into this week's opening ceremony in Glasgow. Cornish artist Bonnie Steward created Team England's Baton from rubbish collected on beaches, riverbanks and in towns in the hope of highlighting the growing threat of ocean plastic.

‌



Her striking artwork will be showcased before King Charles and Queen Camilla at the opening ceremony inside Glasgow's OVO Hydro. The 27-year-old, from Crowntown, near Helston, transformed crisp packets, pieces of fishing rope, fragments of tennis balls and other discarded waste into colourful mosaics depicting England's best-known landmarks and landscapes.

‌



Tower Bridge and the Angel of the North feature alongside coastal views inspired by her Cornish home, with every piece of plastic collected from the places represented in the design.

Steward said: "Literally every single piece, a crisp packet, a part of a tennis ball or a piece of fishing rope, everything you see, I've collected. On the King's Baton, there are pieces from the Thames foreshore, from our own shores and urban areas.

"I hope people understand that ocean plastic is not just a beach issue."

‌



View 2 Images The King's baton designed by Bonnie Steward.

Steward, who founded her BISH ART business in Cornwall, began collecting plastic after becoming increasingly alarmed by the amount of rubbish washing ashore near her home.

She said: "Growing up on the Cornish coastline, I became increasingly saddened by how much plastic was being washed ashore. I started collecting it because I couldn't ignore it, and I quickly became obsessed with beach cleaning."

‌



Her artwork is designed to resemble a painting from a distance, before revealing the individual pieces of waste when viewed up close.

Steward added: "What I like about creating my work is that when people view it, they think it's a painting at first glance. But the closer they look, they notice all the elements. It's almost like a puzzle."

For the first time, each Commonwealth nation received its own baton to personalise ahead of Glasgow 2026. Steward said working on such a small scale presented a new challenge, but she was determined to create something that represented the whole country.

Article continues below

She said: "I've never worked at such a small size before, so every detail had to count.

"What mattered most was creating something people could connect with, something familiar and an artwork that was reflective of England as a whole. As an artist, you rarely imagine your work being carried by athletes across the nation, so to see the Baton out in the world is surreal."

Sports.title: 'Really exciting' - Swimmer Luke Greenbank selected to carry Team England baton at Glasgow 2026 Opening Ceremony
Sports.content:
'Really exciting' - Swimmer Luke Greenbank selected to carry Team England baton at Glasgow 2026 Opening Ceremony

The swimmer is heading to his third Commonwealth Games and will start by leading his country out at the Opening Ceremony

View 2 Images Team England swimmer Luke Greenbank will be carrying the baton at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games opening ceremony. (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Luke Greenbank knows only Commonwealth gold will outdo the honour of being selected as Team England’s baton bearer at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

‌



The 28-year-old will carry his country’s baton at Thursday’s opening ceremony alongside flagbearer Sian Honnor. Greenbank heads to his third Games and after a disappointing showing at Birmingham 2022, where the Olympic bronze medallist missed out on individual honours, the Cockermouth swimmer is confident that his best is yet to come as one of the most experienced members of the swimming squad.

‌



He said: “At Gold Coast, I was the newcomer and didn't really know what to expect. In Birmingham, I probably put too much pressure on myself and didn't get the performances I wanted.

‌



“This time, I feel really confident coming into the Games. I don't put as much pressure on myself anymore and I'm a more experienced athlete. I'll be a bit calmer and hopefully that leads to some good results.

“Compared with my first Games, I'm much more mature and experienced. I understand what a major sporting event looks like and how to handle myself. I've learned a lot from previous Commonwealth Games, Olympics and World Championships. Once you've experienced enough of them, it becomes second nature and you don't feel the same pressure because it's just another swim.

“I've never won an individual Commonwealth medal, so that's a massive aim for me and a really big motivator. I don't want to put too much pressure on that. I just need to focus on what I have to do to produce the best performance possible.”

‌



Greenbank won 4x100m medley silver on the Gold Coast before upgrading to gold in Birmingham but before Greenbank takes to the pool, he will represent his country at the opening ceremony in the new baton-bearer role. It is particularly poignant for Greenbank, having been given the nod by his fellow athletes.

View 2 Images Luke Greenbank.

He added: “To be nominated as flagbearer is really exciting. It's not something swimmers usually get to experience because we're competing from day one, but because my events are a little later in the programme, I'll be able to attend. It'll be a great experience and I'm really proud to represent the team. I knew I had been nominated by Swim England, but I wasn't really expecting anything.

‌



“Then at a team meeting I was told by the Team England staff. It was a really nice moment to be selected by the athletes and represent them at the opening ceremony.”

With the Games taking place in Glasgow, the Cumbrian’s friends and family have a shorter journey than most other English supporters and he is relishing the extra support in his bid for individual glory.

“It's probably closer for me here than Birmingham [2022] was, which is funny,” he said. “It'll be great to have friends and family in the crowd. My mum and dad are coming up, as is my fiancée, Anna. I'm really excited and hopefully I can put on a good show for them.

Article continues below

“The key is to keep a cool head, stick to the race plan and trust the training. Training has been going really well recently, so I can't let anything get into my head too much. The hard work is done now.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa are inviting a nightmare to their door with ludicrous Alejandro Garnacho transfer
Sports.content:
Aston Villa are inviting a nightmare to their door with ludicrous Alejandro Garnacho transfer

Aston Villa have sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea in a record-breaking £117million transfer and as they look to bring in players of their own have turned to Alejandro Garnacho

View 2 Images Unai Emery led Aston Villa into the Champions League but has lost key players this summer (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Aston Villa are about to swing violently from the sublime to the ridiculous. With a decision so bizarre, it feels akin to parking a Robin Reliant where a Ferrari has just been.

‌



Perhaps Unai Emery thinks he can be the manager to release the handbreak belonging to Alejandro Garnacho. What other reason could there be for the Villa manager to think there is some logic to replacing Morgan Rogers with Garnacho?

‌



But the real mistake Emery has made is convincing himself Garnacho is a good footballer in the first place.

‌



There were several reasons Garnacho failed to make the Argentina squad for this summer's World Cup. These included his attitude in training, approach to the game in general and an unhealthy obsession with social media. But the one which stuck out like a sore thumb, was also the one which saw Lionel Messi raise concerns about how disruptive Garnacho is capable of being in a squad and its dressing room.

In short, Emery has invited a nightmare to his own doorstep.

‌



Emery has earned a reputation for reviving lost causes in the past. The likes of Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio spring to mind.

But the Spaniard has bitten off more than he can chew, this time.

When Chelsea agreed to hand over £40m to Manchester United for Garnacho last summer, Sir Jim Ratcliffe was said to be doing a dance of delight around the swimming pool of his mansion on the outskirts of Monaco. The United co-owner must have felt like popping an expensive bottle of the finest French champagne.

‌



He had rid his club of a footballer who had helped inject poison into the Old Trafford dressing room. Someone who personified United's previous indulgences with spoiled brats. A footballer with the ego of Eric Cantona, but the footballing talent of Eric Morecambe.

Villa supporters won't be laughing though. In fact, no-one associated with the club should be.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho has no future at Chelsea under Xabi Alonso (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Garnacho is someone who tries to write cheques his abilities cannot cash. The bright lights of London came calling, but Garnacho remained glued to the dimmer switch.

In a combined 117 league appearances for both United and Chelsea, Garnacho has scored the sum total of 17 goals.

‌



When Chelsea made the mind-boggling decision to sign Garnacho, United's gain was their loss. It summed up the London club's obsession with disfunction and arrogance.

And now, it seems, Emery is about to fall into the same trap.

He cannot seem to see what the rest of football can. The game is about the company you keep, and Emery is about to invite a troublemaker into his ranks. Because the only thing Garnacho is good at is getting managers the sack.

Article continues below

And if this trend continues in Birmingham, then Emery will only have himself to blame.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
